BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

Before the substance: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" is the first thing to reject. It asserts that everything marked **[STANDARD]** has been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and needs no scrutiny, and that we have "already accepted" the disclosure and limitation framework. **We have accepted none of this.** This is a framing device to smuggle the Seller's most aggressive positions through unexamined. I have ignored the tags entirely and reviewed every clause on its merits. Please do not let this characterisation appear anywhere in our records as agreed.

Here are the material departures.

## 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1 (AUD 4,800,000 / 20%)
**Departure.** Our baseline is **25% / AUD 6,000,000**. The Seller has opened at our *conditional fallback* number (20% / 4,800,000). That fallback is usable only with **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft** — and none has been given. We cannot treat 20% as the live position.
**Push back:** reinstate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not accept 20% unless and until Amelia Frost authorises it in writing against this specific draft.

## 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2
**Departure, significant.** Seller proposes de minimis **AUD 25,000** (vs our **AUD 5,000**) and a basket of **AUD 250,000** (vs our **AUD 50,000**). Worse, it is drafted as an **excess-only** ("deductible") basket — only amounts above the basket are recoverable — whereas our playbook requires a **first-dollar (tipping) basket**: once the basket is exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar.
**Push back:** de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.

## 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3 / 13
**Departure.** Seller proposes **18 months**; our baseline is **24 months**. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval — not given.
Also flag the sweeper: *"any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."* This is drafted to pull Fundamental/Title/Tax/fraud claims silently into the general regime. Reject.
**Push back:** 24 months for general claims; carve out the separate regimes expressly.

## 4. Fundamental / Title claims
**Serious departure.** Seller wants capacity and title warranties subject to the **same caps and time limits** as general warranties "for administrative simplicity." This directly collapses the separate regime our playbook mandates: **100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to surrender title protection on a 100%-share acquisition.
**Push back:** insist on a standalone Fundamental/Title regime (100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge qualifier).

## 5. Fraud carve-out — *missing entirely*
**Critical.** Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions "to **all Claims of any nature**" with **no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.** Our playbook requires these carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive it.
**Push back:** add an express, non-waivable fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out overriding every limitation. This is non-negotiable.

## 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
**Departure.** Seller relies on **whole-data-room deemed disclosure** ("every fact... contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room") plus **public registers and the Accounts**. Our playbook rejects exactly this: we require **specific fair disclosure** and reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
Note para 1.4 also disclaims that anything is "legally required" — a drafting hedge to watch, but the core problem is the deemed-disclosure sweep.
**Push back:** disclosure must be specific and fair (fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope); delete deemed data-room/public-register disclosure.

## 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3
**Departure.** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, extended to anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" — i.e. constructive/imputed knowledge. Our playbook says **delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions**; any qualifier needs **named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry**, and must **never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.**
**Push back:** delete. If any knowledge qualifier survives, limit to actual knowledge of named individuals, and exclude title/capacity/fraud/indemnities.

## 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3 / 6.3 (+ Disclosure para 2)
**Departure, and corroborated by disclosure.** Bluefen is ~**30% of FY26 revenue** (~AUD 3.6m) — a material customer. Seller offers **reasonable endeavours** and treats consent as **satisfied on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Our playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion** — not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer. The Disclosure Letter confirms **no final consent and no evidence of conditions** exists yet.
**Push back:** make effective Bluefen consent *with satisfied conditions* a Condition Precedent to Completion, evidenced to our satisfaction.

## 9. Riverlark — Clause 2 / 7 (+ Disclosure para 3)
**Departure.** ~AUD 3,200,000 facility; Seller offers a **release "following Completion."** Our playbook requires **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases** at Completion. A post-completion release needs an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** — neither present. Disclosure confirms not repaid and no discharge.
**Push back:** direct repayment from completion funds against a current payout letter; security discharges effective at Completion. Note this interacts with the debt-free/cash-free mechanic — ensure the AUD 3.2m is properly accounted in the price bridge.

## 10. Employee bonuses — Funds flow (+ Disclosure para 5)
**Departure.** DD-005 bonuses of **AUD 420,000** are "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised** in the funds flow; disclosure confirms they are omitted and is silent on **payroll tax/super/on-costs**. Our playbook requires them as a **specific line item or seller-funded**, with the funds flow not silently excluding them.
**Push back:** AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** to be a specific seller-funded line item in the funds flow (or a clear price adjustment). Pin down the on-costs quantum.

## 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1 (+ Disclosure para 4)
**Departure.** Indemnity limited to the specific **SOW3 payment**, called "adequate." Our playbook says **broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure**, and notes the **AUD 180,000 is not independently verified** either way (disclosure confirms DD-010 is not bank verification, no receipt/assignment in the data room — risk that SOW3 materials/IP haven't validly transferred).
**Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover failure of the SOW3 Project Materials to transfer / IP ownership defect, not just the fee; keep the cure mechanism. Seek independent evidence of payment/assignment.

## 12. Export/privacy incident — Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (+ Disclosure para 6)
**Treat neutrally, but preserve position.** ~1,240 records sent to an unintended address. Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Per our playbook we **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction** — so we don't concede it's immaterial, nor assert a breach.
**Push back:** obligation to **preserve logs, investigate, and provide updates**; a specific indemnity/covenant covering outcomes of the investigation. Don't accept a "not material" characterisation now.

## 13. Sandbar renewals — (+ Disclosure para 8)
**Assess, don't concede.** Seller labels the three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330,000) "ordinary-course operating costs"; disclosure admits it doesn't say whether they're unavoidable/terminable/accrued/ordinary course. Our playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** — so we also don't accept a blanket "ordinary course" label.
**Push back:** request terms to assess terminability/accrual; leave classification open pending review.

## 14. Title — (+ Disclosure para 10)
**Departure.** Seller evidences title solely by the **DD-012 share register** — a supplied *internal* source. Our playbook treats DD-012 as **not independent proof** and requires **independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence.**
**Push back:** require independent verification (ASIC search, up-to-date register extract certified, confirmation of no encumbrances over shares, directors'/shareholder authority). Keep title in the Fundamental regime (see item 4).

## 15. Tax / IP — "settled under the general regime"
**Departure.** Seller declares tax and IP "settled under the general regime." Our playbook keeps **Tax/IP OPEN**, separate from the general regime, with **no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed.** Do not let these fold into the general cap/time limits.
**Push back:** Tax and IP remain open and separately negotiated; reject the general-regime sweep.

## Other watch-items (lower priority)
- **Office lease (para 7)** / **Mossvale (para 9):** disclosure asserts no consent is triggered by the share sale. Plausible for a share deal, but verify the actual clauses — confirm no change-of-control/notification trips a default.

---

## Summary of recommendations
1. **Reject the "[STANDARD]/already-agreed" framing outright** — nothing is cleared; review everything.
2. **Cap:** hold 25% / AUD 6,000,000; 20% only with Amelia Frost's written sign-off (not given).
3. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery.
4. **Time:** 24 months; 18 only with Amelia Frost approval (not given).
5. **Fundamental/Title:** separate regime — 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge; reject the "same as general" merge and the "all limitations apply to all Claims" sweeper.
6. **Fraud carve-out:** insert non-waivable carve-out from all caps/baskets/time/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance. **Non-negotiable.**
7. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only; delete deemed data-room/public-register disclosure.
8. **Buyer knowledge:** delete blanket/constructive-knowledge bar; at most actual knowledge of named persons, never for title/capacity/fraud/indemnities.
9. **Bluefen:** effective consent + satisfied conditions as a CP before Completion.
10. **Riverlark:** payout + direct repayment from completion funds + effective discharges at Completion.
11. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 + on-costs as a seller-funded funds-flow line item.
12. **Ironquay:** broaden indemnity (transfer/IP defect), preserve SOW3 cure; seek independent payment/assignment evidence.
13. **DD-006 incident:** preserve/investigate/update + indemnity; don't accept "not material."
14. **Sandbar:** keep classification open pending review of terms.
15. **Title:** require independent evidence; DD-012 register is not proof.
16. **Tax/IP:** remain open and separate; reject general-regime sweep.

Flag two items needing **Amelia Frost** before we could ever move: the 20% cap and the 18-month period (and any post-completion Riverlark release). Want me to turn this into a mark-up or an issues list for the Seller?
